# Cracktro deck mechanics

Bands, navigation, transitions, audio and animated SVG flows in `docs/public/cracktro/deck.js` (content) and `runtime.js` (engine). Load when changing slide order, groups, transitions, sound or a flow diagram.

- **Bands:** the deck is a table of rows. A slide's `group` is its band: `intro` (title), `platform`, `security`, `mindset` (header-less, like the title and finale), `process`, `trust` (header-less), `cost`, `engineering`, `enterprise`, `cao`, `data`, `finale`. Rows follow each group's first appearance in the source, except that the `finale` row (`last` in `create`) is always moved last, so changing a slide's `group` moves it to that band without moving its code. Generic human/agent process patterns (swimlane flows with `SEQ`/`LANE` that any team can adopt) belong in `process` ("Human agent processes"); named loops that gh-aw runs on itself are worked examples of those patterns and hang in a column below the pattern they instantiate (`under: "<key>"`; kids follow source order, wherever their code sits). Each column head is one documented pattern family, so check `docs/src/content/docs/patterns/` before adding a column or example: `prr` Pull Request Review² (ReviewOps; ↓ Ponytail Reviewer, Issue Monster, Decide · Draft · Record, PR Sous Chef), `improvers` Daily Improvers (DailyOps, ResearchPlanAssignOps; ↓ Repo Assist, Research · Assign · Observe, Hunt · Falsify · Fix, Query · Ask · Grow, Semantic clustering, Go Fan), `dreaming` Dreaming (mining human/agent activity to design and optimize workflows, prompts, skills and linters; ↓ Mine · Refine · Apply, Explore · Reuse · Lint, Scan · Fix · Learn), `specs` Spec-driven testing (SpecOps; ↓ Spec · Model · Test), `docs` Docs that heal (↓ Multi-device tester, Findings that land, Personas · Probe · Patch), `commands` Repo Commands (ChatOps, LabelOps: the synthetic `slash_command` and `label_command` triggers; ↓ LabelOps state machines). Event-driven Hand-offs (IssueOps, DailyOps, ReviewOps, LabelOps) opens the main line, Repo Commands follows it, and Issues as intent (IssueOps) follows Pull Request Review² and Merge fast, unslop daily follows Daily Improvers, all without a column; standalone processes (Speech To Agent, For PMs) close the band's main line; their code sits after the worked examples, before Patch to PR. Columns work in any band: in `platform`, Continuous AI (GitHub Next's definition of the category) hangs under CI/CD meets Continuous AI (`continuous-ai`), and Deliver · Accept · Attribute (one measured pull request) and From Delivery to Value (its full record) hang under Turn Automation into Value (`value`), which Turn Intent into Value (no column) precedes on the main line; in `security`, Model-checked (TLA+/TLC) hangs under Safe outputs (`safe-outputs`); in `engineering`, Skills in review (the Matt Pocock Skills Reviewer, measured) hangs under Skills (`skills`), and Week of daily runs (measured) hangs under Fuzzy schedules (`schedules`). `data` ("AW factory") keeps the measured history slides and Patch to PR. The deck.js `// ---------- bands ----------` block holds `BANDS` (id → header title/subtitle), `SOLO` and `PROTO`; runtime.js `create` builds `rows`, moves each `under` slide right after its `key` parent (setting `s.kids` and `k.parent`; an orphan throws), and inserts a generated header slide (`header: true`, `bh-` classes, one tile per main-line slide (examples omitted; a column head shows a `.bh-k` "↓ N" badge) with `data-go` that wrap into a 7-column grid above 8 slides (10 columns above 14) and use the kicker when a heading exceeds 32 characters, plus a band map) at the start of every band except `intro` and `finale`. `PROTO` (group → product name) marks bands that are not shipped product: every slide of the band, header included, gets a dashed "Research prototype · <name>" badge (`.proto`, top right); `cao` (header "Central Agentic Ops", subtitle "CAO · gh cao", badge "gh cao") is one. Each slide then gets `s.band` and each row `r.start`. Each slide gets a stable `s.id` (explicit `id`, else the heading slug; a duplicate gets `-2`, `-3`) used in `#<id>` hashes; legacy `#N` hashes are rewritten to the id. Positions are absolute and include headers, so adding a slide shifts everything after it: link slides by id, never by number. Only `slides.md` lists slides: add, move or remove the slide's row (with its Id) there (the tests read it) and nothing else; pin an `id` in `deck.js` when a heading is long or likely to change. Headers and slides share their band's `THEME`.
- **Navigation:** three levels: bands, the main line of a band, and columns. Left/Right/Space step along the main line (`nextTop`/`prevTop` skip examples; from an example they continue from its parent) and wrap between bands (Left on a header goes to the last main-line slide of the band above). PageUp/PageDown and Shift+Up/Down call `band(±1)`, which always jumps to the first slide (header) of the band above/below (`rows[b].start`); no per-band cursor is kept. Up/Down and vertical swipes call `vstep(±1)`: inside a column (`colOf(s)`: the head or one of its examples) they walk `[head, ...kids]`, and past either end, or on a slide without a column, they fall back to `band(±1)`. Moves within a column use the vertical up/down transitions. The `.vnb` toolbar button (bottom-right dock, `paintColumn`; no overlay) appears only in a column: lit with a bouncing ↓ and the example count `N` on the head, `i/N` on examples (click steps down), and ↑ "Back to the pattern" on the last example (U jumps to the head from any example). Every button (dock, dialogs, map and header tiles, in-slide controls) has a `title` ending in its shortcut in parentheses, e.g. `(G)` or `(← → switch process)`, and dock buttons also set `aria-keyshortcuts`; a new button needs both plus a key handler (runtime `keydown` or the slide's `onNext`/`onPrev`/`onKey`). Digits then Enter jump to slide N (the dots' shortcut; digits expire after 2 s); slides with a prompt open it with P (a wrapped `onKey`). The dots are a mini-map with one `.drow` per band; column heads get `.col`, examples a narrow `.sub` dot. In the slide map each band is a `section.smp-row` region: an `h3.smp-l` header (band title and `#first–last` range) above a `.smp-tiles` auto-fill grid (tiles at least 150px wide, 2 columns at 640px and below). A column is a `.smp-col` block on the same tracks (`subgrid`) spanning the head plus its examples, capped at the grid's track count (`smpFit`, on open and resize): the head tile (badge `↓N`), then its `.smp-t.sub` examples in a dotted, wrapping `.smp-kids` group labelled "<head> examples". On each open, tiles, headers and rules enter staggered by `--d`, rippling out from the current slide (`smpDelay`, capped at 600 ms); any key finishes the entrance first, and `prefers-reduced-motion` disables it.
- **Tours:** `TOURS` in `deck.js` (after `PROTO`, passed as `tours`) maps a name to `{ title, summary, bands?, slides? }`: whole bands by group id plus individual slide ids. An example rides with its pattern: it stays in a tour only when its column head is in it, so list the head too. `create` warns (`CracktroDeck: tour "<name>" ...`) on unknown bands or ids and on examples without their pattern; a test opens every tour and expects no warning. `#<id>&tour=<name>` opens a tour; `#<id>&view=<payload>` opens a custom view whose payload is base64url JSON `{ t?, b?, s? }` (title, bands, slide ids). In a tour, Left/Right, Up/Down, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown skip hidden slides, dots of hidden slides get `.out`, and a `.tourp` pill shows the title, `i/N` (opens the map, G) and × (leave, X). A move to a hidden slide (digit jump, search, map tile) leaves the tour. The slide map lists tours at its bottom; "Design a view" turns tiles into checkboxes (band header checkboxes toggle a whole band; examples of an unpicked pattern are disabled with `.off`), with a title field, count and copyable `&view=` link. Map keys: T focuses the tours, D toggles design mode; in design mode A selects all, C clears, L copies the link, Ctrl+Enter applies and Esc cancels. Keep tours short, ordered by the deck, and update them when you rename or remove a listed slide.
- **Band themes:** `THEME` (the `// ---------- band themes ----------` block, before bands) is the single source of each band's look and sound; slides never set `sound`, `palette` or `red`. An entry is `{ base, pal, grid: [r,g,b,minorA,majorA], ang, cell, accent, red?, light?, music, prog }`: background fill, four glow colours, grid colour and alphas, grid angle, minor cell size (major lines every 5 cells), header colours, the red security wash (`go()` covers entry with it), the `MUSIC` key played on entering every slide of the band, and per-step semitone shifts (`prog[step % length]`) so the band's music varies along it. Current bands: intro and platform share GitHub brand green 15°, security dark red wash 45°, mindset and trust are soft grey (#c8d1da) concept slides with no grid (`light: true` sets `body.light`, which darkens slide text and the nav chrome; `go()` stages any light/dark switch: the old slide fades out, the background swaps, then the new slide enters), process blueprint blue 0°, cost gold -45°, engineering purple 30°, enterprise metallic grey -30° (wide cells), cao (Central Agentic Ops, research prototype) deep teal 60°, data violet 0° (fine cells), finale neutral. Other bands use a distinct hue and orientation; the background, grid angle and cell size ease between bands. The background canvas draws fill and glows at quarter resolution and repaints the grid only when it changes. Keep body text #e6edf3 ≥ 7:1 and muted #8b949e ≥ 4:1 against the brightest glow overlap.
- **Transitions:** derived from `group`. Siblings in a band use a reveal-style horizontal push (`slide-in`/`slide-out`); `show()` sets `--dx` to `100%` going forward, `-100%` going back, and `0%` on first load. Crossing into another band slides up (`up-in`/`up-out`) going forward and down (`down-in`/`down-out`) going back. All use the same 0.8 s curve. Every slide needs a `group`; never add per-slide transition overrides. The old slide keeps the `.leaving` class until a timeout clears it.
- **Audio isolation:** `sfx` methods: `slide, band, step, cut, techno, pop, key, compile, review, notify, omen, route, mr, toggle, unlock`. `master` is a persistent gain that feeds the compressor and delay. `out` is a per-slide bus. `show()` calls `sfx.cut()`, which fades the current bus and replaces it, so long themes cannot leak into the next slide. Any new sound must connect to `out`, or to `master` if it must persist across slides (as techno does).
- **CSS animations restart** through `void el.offsetWidth` before `.active` is added. Prefer `.active .x { animation: ... }` for entry effects. Hidden slides keep their DOM (`visibility: hidden`); the runtime pauses their CSS animations (pseudo-elements included) until they are shown again, but not timers, rAF loops or `el.animate()` animations (`perf.md`).
- **Animated SVG flow diagrams** (for example "Daily Improvers"):
  - Built with helpers such as `agent()`, `dev()`, `box()`, `codeScan()` and `ico()`.
  - `EDGES` entries are `[id, svgPath, class, labelLines, lx, ly, anchor]`.
  - `SEQ` entries are `[edgeId|null, nodeLitOnArrival, durationMs?]`.
  - `LANE` maps each node to its lane.
  - The loop length is `START + steps * STEP + HOLD`.
  - On cycle reset, `.on`, `.hot` and `.seen` are removed from the whole SVG, so keep any persistent state (such as counters) outside those classes.
- **Repeated ids:** several slides reuse ids such as `nIssue`, `nDev1` and `nDev2`, and constants such as `HOLD`. When editing, make `old_str` unique by including nearby slide-specific context.
